author: marketing_c
protectedRevelations: Four-future comparisons and preferred institutional prescription

scenes.title: The career and the family
scenes.viewerPurpose: Recognize a rewarded career making family life difficult Ask what choices society quietly favors
scenes.composition: Career success shares the frame with a long journey home
addOrChange: Remove prestige ledgers and add one realistic clock.

cues.narration: A society rewards a career, then makes it difficult to build a family around it.
cues.visualAction: A work reward arrives as available family time shrinks.

cues.narration: The Society That Selects Us examines the quiet filters inside that contradiction.
cues.visualAction: Keep workplace and home connected through the long route.

scenes.title: The same wish
scenes.viewerPurpose: See housing work and care shape future possibilities Picture equally willing parents facing unequal costs
scenes.composition: Two people want the same family life under unequal conditions
addOrChange: Add identical wish notes and no rankings or genetic symbols.

cues.narration: Housing, work, care, and prestige shape which ways of life remain possible across generations.
cues.visualAction: Show nearby care against repeated moving and commuting.

cues.narration: Two people may want children equally while facing very different costs of becoming parents.
cues.visualAction: Set the identical wishes beside different practical costs.

scenes.title: Which lives are possible
scenes.viewerPurpose: Understand these are not claims of fixed genetic destiny See research brought back to everyday settings
scenes.composition: A parent and planner compare possible support arrangements
addOrChange: Remove genetic implications and keep observations separate from hypotheses.

cues.narration: It examines those differences without treating people’s futures as fixed by their genes.
cues.visualAction: Change support around the person while keeping the person unchanged.

cues.narration: It brings research about personality into everyday questions about cities, communities, and technology.
cues.visualAction: Review distances and care as research questions around the household.

scenes.title: Across generations
scenes.viewerPurpose: Notice praise and support pulling in opposite directions Ask which lives our institutions make possible
scenes.composition: A reader connects present work with passing on a valued practice
addOrChange: Add adult and child sharing a skill, without fertility scoring.

cues.narration: A culture can celebrate a way of life while making it hard to pass on.
cues.visualAction: Show the skill being shared despite constrained time.

cues.narration: What are our institutions encouraging us to become, and which futures do they make difficult to continue?
cues.visualAction: Hold the household beside the institutional choices shaping it.
